rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: # Plant breeding — methods and examples ## 1. Introduction Opening frame for **Plant breeding — methods and examples** — what the topic is, why it matters, a real-world hook (Nepal where possible), the map of what follows, and the learning outcomes (biology-plan.md §3.1, block I). Prose depth is written in the Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production fill pass. ## 2.…  ·  **Plant breeding** is the purposeful genetic improvement of crop plants: cross parents carrying desirable traits, select the best offspring over generations, and release a stable, superior variety. The classic steps: collection of germplasm → hybridisation → selection → testing → release. Success stories: high-yielding wheat and rice of the Green Revolution, and fortified crops like iron-rich spinach varieties.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Six-step classical protocol: collection of variability → evaluation and selection of parents → cross-hybridisation → selection of superior recombinants → testing/release (multi-year field trials) — the ordered list IS the answer.  ·  Trick 2: Examples: semi-dwarf wheat (Norman Borlaug, Sonalika/Kalyan Sona), rice (Jaya, IR-8), sugarcane (Saccharum × Saccharum barbari), millets hybrid — quote two.
